newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina investment grade distant - ING Barings.
newsitem.headline: Argentina investment grade distant - ING Barings.

text.p: Argentina's economic and fiscal performance is still not good enough to warrant a swift rise in its risk rating to investment grade, a senior ING Barings economist said Tuesday.

Arturo Porzecanski, ING Barings' head of fixed-income research and chief economist for the Americas, told a bankers convention here that Argentina still had a chronic budget deficit pushing up its foreign debt.
"I don't see any immediate progress towards a balanced budget," he said.
He added that the government was continuing to rely too much on tapping credit markets in foreign currencies rather than opting for pesos.

"I see the development of the debt paper market in pesos, especially for the long term, as very slow, not very well thought out," Porzecanski said, "The emphasis seems to be on taking advantage of whatever is cheaper and not on what is a good idea for the future."
While Argentina's exports have grown strongly in recent years, their future growth is not guaranteed, and could be seriously compromised by any crisis in Brazil, he added.
Argentina's overall debt level is "extremely high", and far too high a proportion of it is in foreign currency, he said.

All this comes on top of Argentina's recently reformed, but historically "dreadful" debt performance, said Porzecanski, who finished his speech with the words, "If we are objective Argentina still has some way to go before it is investment grade."
Risk raters Standard & Poor's recently raised Argentina's long-term foreign currency debt to BB from BB-, although competitor Moody's kept Argentina at B1.
